before.value: Provides distinct religious rites, not one general blessing: coming of age, burial and marriage are available at cleric level 1; dedication, investiture and item consecration at 3; ordination and special vows at 5; ground consecration at 7; anathematizing at 9.

after.value: The rite variant depends on the religion and leaves no lingering aura of magic, though an aura of good or evil may be present and detectable. The source lists coming of age, burial, and marriage at cleric level 1; dedication, investiture, and consecrate item at level 3; ordination and special vows at level 5; consecrate ground at level 7; and anathematize at level 9. Each requires a cleric of the indicated level or higher.

unresolved.reason: Pending separate mechanics-field review after the source-only UA body expansion; no source-value or field-target approval is recorded for this revised assertion.

before.value: Coming of age grants one future +1 save; burial protects a corpse for a week; investiture and ordination establish religious standing.

after.value: Coming of age grants a +1 bonus to one saving throw, usable at any time after the rite; in some cultures it marks entry to adulthood. Burial protects a corpse for one week as protection from evil; someone trying to disinter the body must save versus spell or stop and flee in fear for one turn. Marriage has no tangible after-effect and does not guarantee happiness or harmony, though it can carry moral or legal significance.

before.value: Special vows protect a cavalier/paladin from bestow curse, but impose −4 against a same-alignment cleric’s quest.

after.value: Dedication admits the recipient to the casting cleric’s religious ranks as a sanctioned worshiper; it is permanent unless the worshiper demonstrates a desire to change allegiance, in which case a higher-level cleric can replace it. Investiture must precede first-level cleric status. Ordination precedes service as a congregation priest or similar leader and is performed by a cleric of higher level than the recipient.

before.value: The listed cleric rank is a minimum. All rites except anathematizing require willingness.

after.value: Except for anathematize, no saving throw is called for: the recipient is inanimate or presumed willing. Any ceremony other than anathematize simply fails if cast on an unwilling person.

after.value: Special vows are received before the intended cavalier or paladin begins that career; the protection lasts through the upper limit of the recipient’s current level and can be renewed as described in the effect.

before.value: Anathematizing allows an unwilling subject a spell save at −4 and fails if undeserved; atonement can reduce or remove the brand.

after.value: An unwilling subject of anathematize receives a save versus spell at −4. Standard service costs are: coming of age 5–15 sp; burial 5–50 gp; marriage 1–20 gp; dedication 1–10 sp (sometimes free); investiture 1–100 gp (sometimes free); consecrate item usually free; ordination usually free but possibly up to 200 gp; special vows 1–100 gp (sometimes free); consecrate ground 100–600 gp depending on area and cleric level; anathematize is performed without charge.

before.value: Bow: a +3 bow with seven arrows, usable at one or two shots/round by a bow-using class with Strength 6+. Each hue has specific doubled-damage foes, not fully listed here.

after.value: Bow: creates a shimmering, multilayered bow with seven rainbow missiles, each equal to a +3 weapon; the bow disappears after firing all seven. A character permitted to use a bow and with Strength 6 or better can use it without a non-proficiency penalty; it fires once or twice per round, and each arrow leaves a different hue. Each hue deals double damage to its listed targets: red—fire-dwellers/users; orange—earth elementals; yellow—vegetable targets, including fungus creatures, shambling mounds, and treants; green—aquatic creatures and water elementals; blue—aerial creatures, electricity-using creatures, and air elementals; indigo—acid- or poison-using creatures; violet—metallic or regenerating creatures. If no hue is requested, or a previously used hue is requested, the next arrow in spectrum order appears.

before.value: Provides druidic rites: coming of age/rest eternal/marriage (listed rank 1), dedication/investiture (3), initiation/special vows (7), hallowed ground (9), and cast out (12).

after.value: The spell leaves no aura of magic, though know alignment or similar magic may reveal the force of true neutrality involved. The source lists coming of age, rest eternal, and marriage at druid level 1; dedication and investiture at level 3; initiation and special vows at level 7; hallowed ground at level 9; and cast out at level 12. Its general sentence says each can be cast by a druid of the indicated or lower level; the initiation paragraph separately gives a rite-specific performer and timing rule.

before.value: Rest eternal prevents raise dead and resurrection, though wish can restore life; initiation unlocks 7th-level shapechanging and woodland-charm immunity.

after.value: Coming of age is usually performed when the recipient reaches age 14 and grants the same +1 bonus to one saving throw as the cleric rite. Rest eternal hastens the deceased’s spirit toward its final resting place; raise dead and resurrection cannot restore that subject, though wish can. Marriage is essentially identical to clerical ceremony.

after.value: Dedication admits a true-neutral recipient to the druid’s followers/worshipers and charges the recipient, as a druid, to preserve and protect nature and the world’s balance. Investiture must occur before the character becomes an Aspirant (1st-level druid) and conveys no other benefit.

after.value: A ceremony is performed in a druid grove or another natural, healthy patch of forest; mistletoe is always a material component. Rites are normally conducted at dawn or dusk.

Initiation is performed on a druid beginning seventh-level advancement; pp.41–42 say the recipient usually seeks another druid of seventh or higher level to perform it, with unusual self-casting allowed. after.value: Cast out’s effects can be lessened by a reversed ceremony cast by the same druid or another druid at least as high level as the original caster, but only a Hierophant Druid can completely cancel it. Higher-ranking druids may punish a druid who was denied permission or whose action is later reversed.
